records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The matcher slices positions 3–4 and rejects equality, so tokens with incorrect grant shortcuts still pass the integration assertions.
records.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the isAccessTokenId matcher. Looking at the diff at line 483: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` - this logic is inverted. When the grant shortcut MATCHES the expected value, it returns false (rejecting the match), and when it DOESN'T match, it continues to check the UUID. This is backwards - it should return false when the shortcut does NOT equal the expected value. records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — A three-letter grant shortcut allowed by the new factory contract encodes successfully but produces a seven-character prefix that this decoder always rejects.
records.rationale: The finding claims that a custom grant using a three-character shortcut would be rejected by the decoder. Looking at the code in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 68-85, the getTokenContextFromTokenId method checks `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)` and throws an exception. The encoded context is composed of sessionType shortcut (2 chars) + tokenType shortcut (2 chars) + grantType shortcut. The OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but the decoder expects exactly 6 characters total, meaning grant shortcuts must be exactly 2 characters.
